inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (71.3M; XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding Apr-Jun 2026). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow SBC add-back $23.8M plus $2.8M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement (financing activities); West publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.0 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.2%; essentially unlevered (debt $203M vs ~$26B market cap) so WACC ~ cost of equity; 9.0% used for all three scenarios so risk is charged once via the scenario weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease rent sits inside operating expenses, so it is already inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt (one treatment). lease_cost_pct_path left at 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: US operating company - pharma packaging/delivery components manufacturer). First valuation of WST, no prior DCF. FY0 = FY2025 actuals; year 1 = FY2026, anchored to the raised guidance (net sales $3.345-3.380B, capex $250-275M, Q2 2026 call 23-Jul-2026). EBITDA margin paths are PRE-SBC (GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC): FY2019 23.1%, FY2021 32.2% (COVID vaccine peak), FY2023 28.4%, FY2025 25.4%, H1 2026 27.1% GAAP; Q2 2026 is ~29.3% on the adjusted basis (adj EPS $2.37 vs GAAP $2.17, ~$19M pre-tax restructuring/SmartDose costs). FY2026 guided adj EPS $8.85-9.05 implies ~30% pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA; the base path uses 27.6% for FY2026, GAAP basis with restructuring still in it, then converges to 30.5%. Interest income NOT stripped: WST reports interest net, net cash at 30-Jun-2026 is $233M (~0.5x the $442M owner-FCF base, below the 1x materiality rule) after $454M of H1 buybacks, and the component build starts from operating EBITDA, which excludes interest. Buybacks are real and large ($1.9B FY2021-H1 2026; $454.3M H1 2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention. Equity bridge adds SmartDose 3.5mL sale proceeds received 1-Jul-2026 (after the balance-sheet date). Working capital is negative capture: receivables $712M + inventory $447M against payables $253M at 30-Jun-2026 (~27% of TTM revenue), so growth consumes cash; incremental capture set at -15% because FY2025 OCF benefited from a ~$100M working-capital release. Price as of the 2-Oct-2026 regular close is within 6% of the 52-week high.

equity_bridge.item: SmartDose 3.5mL sale to AbbVie, proceeds received 1-Jul-2026 (net of est. tax)
equity_bridge.note: $112.5M gross per Q2 2026 release; ~$12.5M tax on gain assumed (book value of transferred assets not in the data at hand). Received after the 30-Jun-2026 balance-sheet date, so not in net cash; the forfeited revenue (~$40M H2 2026) is already excluded from guidance and from the growth path.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (11.4%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (7.4%). Book value is distorted by $1.9B of buybacks since FY2021 and by the FY2021 COVID earnings spike, so revenue CAGR is the selected anchor; the 3-year rates (revenue 2.1%, EPS -4.6%) are depressed by the FY2023-24 post-COVID destocking trough and are not a forward guide either.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes) 5yr CAGR 11.4% EXCEEDS reported FCF CAGR 9.5% because SBC + withholding fell from $39.9M (FY2020) to $26.6M (FY2025) while FCF rose; SBC is not consuming the growth. FY2023-24 FCF was depressed by a 12-13%-of-revenue capex cycle (FY2024 capex $377M) that has since normalized to ~8%.

base.narrative: FY2026 at the raised guidance midpoint; high-single-digit organic growth through FY2030 on HVP components (GLP-1, biologics) and the Annex 1 upgrade cycle, net of a further ~1pp SmartDose roll-off in FY2027; pre-SBC EBITDA margin rebuilds from a GAAP-basis 27.6% (FY2026 still carries SmartDose-exit restructuring, ~2pp in Q2) to 30.5%, between the pre-COVID 23% and the FY2021 COVID peak of 32.2%.

bull.narrative: GLP-1 injectables stay early-stage for years and HVP components keep growing high-teens; Annex 1 conversions of the ~6bn-component installed base pull mix toward HVP; double-digit growth through FY2029 and margin exceeds the FY2021 COVID peak, reaching 33%.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance, then a FY2023-24-style customer destock plus oral GLP-1 formulations and GLP-1 pricing pressure cut HVP volume growth to mid-single digits; capacity built for GLP-1 runs under-utilized and margin stalls near 27.5% (the FY2024-26 GAAP range).

scenario_narratives.base: West keeps compounding at roughly its 10-year pace (~8% revenue CAGR FY2015-25). FY2026 lands at the raised guidance midpoint ($3.36B, 9.4% reported, 10-11% organic). From FY2027 growth stays high-single-digit on HVP components for biologics and injectable GLP-1s, and on the EU Annex 1 sterility upgrade cycle. That is partly offset in FY2027 by the remaining half-year of SmartDose 3.5mL roll-off and a lower-growth West Vantage contract-manufacturing segment. Mix shift toward HVP rebuilds pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 27.6% (GAAP basis, still carrying FY2026 SmartDose-exit restructuring) to 30.5%, which roughly matches Q2 2026 on an adjusted basis and stays short of the FY2021 COVID-vaccine peak of 32.2%. Capex falls from the guided 7.8% of sales to a 6% maintenance-plus-growth level as the GLP-1 capacity build completes.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are GLP-1 and Annex 1. Injectable GLP-1 adoption is still early-stage, as management says, and HVP GLP-1 components keep growing in the high teens. Biologics organic growth (29% in Q2 2026) holds above 15%. The ~6 billion-component Annex 1 opportunity converts Standard Products to higher-spec HVP at higher price points. Revenue grows 10%+ through FY2029, and margin reaches 33% as HVP rises from ~64% of sales toward 75%, above the FY2021 peak. Regulatory switching costs protect each design win for the life of the drug.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are concentration and the delivery format. A small set of GLP-1 makers are a large share of incremental demand. Oral semaglutide/orforglipron formulations and GLP-1 price cuts slow injectable volume growth, while pharma customers destock as they did in FY2023-24, when revenue fell 2% and EBITDA margin compressed ~5pp. Growth drops to 4-5% after FY2026, the capacity built for GLP-1 runs under-utilized, and margin stalls at 27.5%. The market's ~40x forward multiple de-rates; the terminal is capped at 16x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear at 20%, above the 15% default: a material share of incremental growth depends on a handful of GLP-1 customers and on injectables staying the dominant format, and the FY2023-24 destock shows how fast demand can swing. Base at 50%: it tracks raised guidance and the 10-year revenue CAGR. Bull at 30%, below the 35% default: it needs GLP-1, biologics and Annex 1 to all keep delivering, and the price already sits near the 52-week high.

valuation_philosophy.summary: West is a high-quality, regulatory-moated compounder: its components are written into drug filings, so customers rarely switch. At a price near the 52-week high the market is paying for sustained high-single to low-double-digit growth plus margin recovery. The DCF charges SBC and withholding taxes as cash, holds the share count flat (buybacks fund it), and treats working capital as a use of cash for a manufacturer. It caps the terminal at 20x owner FCF for the base and bull cases.
key_risks_to_valuation: GLP-1 concentration: a few drug makers drive much of the HVP growth, and oral formulations could cut injectable volumes.
Customer destocking cycles like FY2023-24 swing revenue and margin hard, since the business has high operating leverage.
Terminal value is most of the value, so the result is sensitive to WACC: each 1pp on the discount rate moves base value by roughly 15-20%.
Capex intensity: if the GLP-1/biologics capacity build keeps capex near the FY2023-24 12-13% instead of normalizing to ~6-7%, owner FCF falls well short of this path.
SmartDose divestiture after-tax proceeds are estimated; the gain and its tax were not disclosed in the data at hand.
